To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the plant hormone auxin regulates gene expression in the rhizobia and that this may affect the symbiosis.

(1) the addition of the plant hormone IAA to Rhizobium cultures induces the expression of genes involved in the interaction with plants, (2) the addition of IAA to Rhibzobium cultures increases their ability to attach to plant roots, and (3) the IAA-regulated genes are involved in the attachment to roots and motility, which are key steps in the legume–rhizobia symbiosis.
IAA regulates the expression of several rhizobial genes that appear to be involved either in plant signal transduction or in attachment to plant roots.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the phytohormone IAA in the rhizosphere.
the study of the role of indole-3 acetic acid (IA A) on Rhizobium-plant interactions.
the role of auxins in the legume–Rhizobium symbioses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IAA is an important signaling molecule in the rhizobial partner of the legume-Rizobium interaction.
the auxin IAA plays a role in the regulation of rhizobial genes, which are involved in motility, attachment to plant roots and the processing of plant signals.
the IAA produced by rhizobia is not a signal for the plant partner, but rather an adaptation strategy for the bacteria to survive and compete in the complex environment of the rhizosphere.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

IAA regulates a set of genes in R. etli that are involved in motility, attachment and signal processing and that these genes are differentially expressed when R. etli is in the rhizosphere of its plant host.
the IAA biosynthesis pathway is a key factor for the interaction of Rhizobiales with plants.
IAA is a plant hormone that is also produced by bacteria, which can affect the expression of genes involved in bacterial motility, attachment to plant roots and processing of plant signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IAA is not a universal plant signal for all rhizobia.
IAA has a role in Rhizobial biology and that this role is distinct from its known role in plant biology.
IAA has a clear effect on gene expression in R. etli, and that this effect is dependent on the growth conditions.
